claims.evidence: The report shows a keyboard labeled “PSR-550”, but it does not show it being powered on or tested (no working keys/display/sound).
The report includes a sticker/label near the control panel that reads “PSR-550”, not PSR-650.

risks.risk: Not actually working (no proof of power-on, functioning keys, display, buttons, or speaker output).
risks.proof: A short video clip showing the keyboard powered on, the display turning on, pressing multiple keys, and playing a sound through the built-in speakers (or headphone output) with volume change.
risks.if_unproven: Price as non-tested/possibly not working (worst-case) until a power-on + sound test is shown.

risks.risk: Model mismatch (PSR-550 vs PSR-650) affecting value and buyer expectations.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the model number from the official label/plate (not just a sticker), plus the exact model shown in the settings/about screen if available.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lower-value/safer assumption based on the visible “PSR-550” label.

risks.risk: Missing accessories (power adapter, sustain pedal, cables) or inability to connect.
risks.proof: Photos showing all included items: power adapter, sustain pedal, and any cables; plus a clip demonstrating the adapter connected and the unit powering on.
risks.if_unproven: Price as incomplete (no accessories) until the adapter/pedal are confirmed.

risks.risk: Key condition issues (sticking keys, broken keys, uneven action) not visible in a single exterior photo.
risks.proof: A video showing a full octave/key sweep (left to right) and repeated pressing of problem-prone keys, ideally with on-screen indicators responding.
risks.if_unproven: Price as potentially worn keys until key-by-key behavior is demonstrated.

risks.risk: Hidden internal faults (speaker distortion, button/display faults, power supply issues) not visible externally.
risks.proof: A clip playing multiple tones/styles with volume up and down, showing stable display/button response; include a quick check of speaker output quality (no crackling/distortion).
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst-case for electronics (possible faults) until functional audio/display testing is shown.

risks.risk: Cosmetic wear/damage (dust/scratches) may indicate heavier use or poor handling, reducing resale value.
risks.proof: Additional photos from multiple angles under good light (including close-ups of the display and keybed area) to assess severity of scratches/damage.

proof_requests: Power-on video: display on, buttons working, and at least a short melody played through built-in speakers (or headphone output).
Clear close-up of the official model label/plate (and/or the model shown in the keyboard’s About/Settings screen).
Photos of included accessories: power adapter and sustain pedal (and any cables).
Video showing key sweep (left-to-right) and repeated pressing to confirm no sticking/broken keys.
Audio test clip showing volume increase/decrease and checking for distortion/crackling.
response.reason: The report identifies a keyboard labeled “PSR-550,” but there is no proof it powers on or produces sound, and the seller’s “working perfectly” claim is unverified. Also, the seller’s PSR650 claim conflicts with the visible PSR-550 label, so confirmation is needed before pricing.
